titles.title: FarCry
titles.engine: CryEngine 1 - Far Cry 1.4 (GOG 2.0.0.9, FileVersion 1.4.0.1405), Direct3D9 renderer Bin32\XRenderD3D9.dll
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080x32 fullscreen on the 1080p LCDs, and the mechanism is present and correct in the staged tree. 'Play Far Cry.bat' copies System-fleet.cfg over System.cfg, calls FLEETRES.BAT, then runs FLEETRES -setline System.cfg r_Width/r_Height = `%FR_W%`/`%FR_H%` (the values stay quoted, which the engine requires). gameres.h lines 773-774 write the same values at GAMESYNC. Measured on .145: C:\Games\FarCry\log.txt (2026-08-30) reads 'Lua cvar: (r_Width,1920)', 'Best-match display mode: 1920x1080x32 (Error=8)' and 'Current Resolution: 1920x1080x32 Full Screen', and the live System.cfg has r_Width = "1920". The 2026-08-31 perbox screenshots show the main menu at 1920x1080 on .123, .240 and .246 (now .195).
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver. The Options > Video 'Resolution' combo (FCData/Scripts.pak SCRIPTS/MenuScreens/Options/Video.lua, widget_resolution.user.Initialize) is filled from System:EnumDisplayFormats() and filtered only by `DispFmt.bpp == 32 and DispFmt.width > 640 and DispFmt.height > 480`. Entries are labelled 'WxHx32' and the default is 1024x768x32. The renderer's EnumDisplayFormats (XRenderD3D9.dll 0x3806cef2-0x3806cfb4) copies every adapter mode {w,h,bpp} and maps 24-bit to 32. It applies no size or aspect filter. That same adapter list contains 1920x1080: the .145 log reads 'Maximum Resolution: 1920x1080'.
titles.evidence: Staged: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/FarCry/Play Far Cry.bat, System-fleet.cfg, FCData/Scripts.pak (Options/Video.lua lines 617-667). agent/shared/gameres.h:773-774. Disassembly: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/farcry_enumdisplayformats_disasm.txt. Box evidence: .../145_FarCry_log.txt and .../145_FarCry_System.cfg (DOWNLOADed 2026-09-29), plus perbox-2026-08-31_123_FarCry_Play_Far_Cry.png and perbox-2026-08-31_246_FarCry_Play_Far_Cry.png (both 1920x1080). GAMERES on .123/.145/.195/.240 lists 1920x1080@60: .../gameres_*_2026-09-29.json.
titles.fix_source: already in tree (Play Far Cry.bat + FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT + System-fleet.cfg; gameres.h rule)
titles.fix_risk: None for the menu. By design the launcher resets System.cfg at every start, so a resolution picked in the menu only lasts one session. Native TCP/IP multiplayer does not depend on resolution.
titles.hw_check: On .145 or .123 (XP, where GDI can capture fullscreen D3D): EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\FarCry" "Play Far Cry.bat", wait about 60 s, then SCREENSHOT 0 should show the 1920x1080 main menu. DOWNLOAD C:\Games\FarCry\log.txt and look for 'Current Resolution: 1920x1080x32 Full Screen'. Menu path: Options > Video > Resolution combo, which should list 1920x1080x32. The widgets carry tabstop attributes (Options.lua tabstop 101-104; UISystemUtils nav buttons 10001+), so Tab/Enter navigation is likely but unverified. The cursor is the engine's own, driven by DirectInput, so absolute UICLICK is not expected to land. Keyboard-only proof of the list (the console Lua prefix is from engine knowledge, not verified here): UIKEY TILDE, then UIKEY TEXT:#for i,f in System:EnumDisplayFormats() do System:Log(f.width.."x"..f.height.."x"..f.bpp) end, then DOWNLOAD log.txt and look for 1920x1080x32. On .195 (Win7) rely on log.txt, not a screenshot.
titles.verifier_notes: Launch at 1080p is measured (log plus screenshots). That the menu lists 1920x1080 is inferred from the Lua filter and renderer code together with the renderer's own logged mode list; no one has seen the combo on screen yet.

titles.title: BF1942
titles.engine: Refractor 1 - Battlefield 1942 v1.61b (BF1942.exe md5 a56d63e83eb5e02b43e1928cb22cd15a, PE 2004-10-19, D3D8), rebuilt from EA 1.6.19 + 1.61b patches; SafeDisc 2.80.010 on Mods\bf1942\Mod.dll
titles.launch_sets: The launchers write 1920x1080, but the client never runs on this fleet. 'Play Battlefield 1942.bat' (lines 54-59) and 'Join Battlefield 1942 - LAN.bat' (lines 27-32) call FLEETRES and then -setline 'game.setGameDisplayMode %FR_W% %FR_H% 32 0' into Mods\bf1942\Settings\Profiles\Default\Video.con and Profiles\Custom\Video.con. gameres.h:770-771 do the same at sync. This is present and correct: .145's deployed files both read 'game.setGameDisplayMode 1920 1080 32 0' (downloaded 2026-09-29). The renderer's setVideoMode lookup (0x63dc40) does an exact w,h,bpp match over the full adapter list with no aspect filter, so 1920x1080x32 should be accepted. However, no fleet box has ever reached a render. SafeDisc 2.80.010 raises 'Cannot locate the CD-ROM' even with the image correctly mounted (measured 2026-08-31 on .124, .133, .143, .240 and .246). The LAN host shortcut is a console dedicated server with no display mode.
titles.menu_source: The driver list passes through a hardcoded aspect filter. The Options/Video 'DisplayModeList' builder (BF1942.exe 0x6b0833-0x6b09e6) lists a renderer mode only if either 0x45f8d0 is true (w == 4*h, the Matrox TripleHead 4:1 test) or (float)h/(float)w == 0.75 (the double at 0x8dbfa0; `test ah,44h / jp skip`), and also w >= 640 (0x280) and h >= 480 (0x1e0). Entries are formatted '%dx%dx%d @ %d' or '%dx%dx%d'. 1920x1080 (0.5625) is never listed, and neither is 1280x1024 (0.8).
titles.evidence: Disassembly: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/bf1942_options_video_4x3_filter_disasm.txt. Box files: .../145_BF1942_Profiles_Default_Video.con and .../145_BF1942_Profiles_Custom_Video.con. Staged launchers under /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/BF1942/. The staged presets Mods/bf1942/Settings/Default/VideoLow.con, VideoMedium.con and VideoHigh.con each contain 'game.setGameDisplayMode 800 600 ...' and are run by the menu code (string refs at 0x6af954 and 0x6b00e9, next to the list builder). SafeDisc wall: compat DB rows for BF1942 on .124/.133/.143/.240/.246 (fleetbook.db compat_render, 2026-08-31).
titles.fix: The in-game list cannot show 1080p without patching EA's exe. The smallest patch is one byte in BF1942.exe at file offset 0x2b08d6 (VA 0x6b08d6): 0x75 becomes 0xEB, turning `jne 0x6b090f` into `jmp` past the 4:3 test, so every adapter mode of at least 640x480 is listed, including 1920x1080. Separately, remove the 'game.setGameDisplayMode 800 600 ...' line from Settings/Default/VideoLow.con, VideoMedium.con and VideoHigh.con (or have the launchers -setline them per box). Otherwise changing the Performance preset in the menu drops the box to 800x600. Neither change can be tested until the SafeDisc 2.80.010 client wall is solved, which needs the pressed disc or a mounter that emulates 2.80.
titles.fix_source: Byte patch made by hand; nothing on the share (searched case-insensitively for bf1942 widescreen/fix; Game Updates holds only the 1.6.19 and 1.61b patches). The preset edits are to files already in the tree.
titles.fix_risk: The patch modifies EA's own BF1942.exe: the md5 changes, which breaks README-FLEET's promise that every executable is EA's own. It must never be combined with the no-CD crack that was deliberately stripped. Multiplayer: PunkBuster is not staged and the fleet's LAN dedicated server does not check client binaries, so there is no LAN impact; an Internet server with PB enabled would kick a modified exe. 16:9 at the staged renderer.fieldOfView may look stretched (unverified).
titles.hw_check: This is currently impossible on every box because the client stops at SafeDisc. Once a client can start: after the launcher runs, DOWNLOAD Profiles\Default\Video.con and Profiles\Custom\Video.con (both should read 1920 1080 32 0). On XP, SCREENSHOT the main menu, which should be 1920x1080. Then open Options > Video and screenshot the display-mode list. BF1942 draws its own cursor; keyboard navigation is not established, so if absolute clicks do not land it needs a human once.
titles.verifier_notes: The compat DB's '.123 n/a: no mounter' row is stale: HWPROFILE now reports disc_mount=true (d347bus) on .123. It makes no difference here, because 2.80 is past what DAEMON Tools 3.47 emulates.

titles.title: MaxPayne
titles.engine: MAX-FX - Max Payne retail v1.05 (in-exe stamp 'Thu Jan 17 09:49:00 2002'), D3D8 via e2driver\e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll; SafeDisc 2.51.020
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080x32, set in the registry, and correct in the staged tree. 'Play Max Payne.bat' (mount template, lines 54-57) calls FLEETRES and then -reg HKCU 'Software\Remedy Entertainment\Max Payne\Video Settings' Display Width=%FR_W% and Display Height=%FR_H%, then starts MaxPayne.exe -nodialog -skipstartup. gameres.h:751-752 write the same values after install.reg, which pins 800x600x32. Read back 2026-09-29 on .123, .145, .195 and .240: Display Width 1920, Display Height 1080, Display Bits Per Pixel 32. This key is proven to be the one the engine reads, because .133 rendered FLEETRES's 1280x960 rather than install.reg's 800x600. On a 1080p LCD it has not been seen rendering: the 2026-08-31 perbox 'verified 1920x1080' row for .246 is a desktop-only frame. Launching also needs SafeDisc 2.51.020 satisfied, which means DAEMON Tools 3.47 with Emulation > SafeDisc turned on. .123 and .145 report d347bus, but the emulation setting on each box is unknown. .195 has only WinCDEmu, which emulates nothing.
titles.menu_source: The in-game VIDEO page offers only 'Texture Sharpness' and 'Brightness' (x_english.ras GCID_VIDEO block), so there is no resolution entry in game. Resolution is chosen only in the pre-game startup dialog (MainDialog: 'Video Settings' with '&Display Adapter:', '&Screen Mode:' and '&Acceleration:'). Its Screen Mode list comes from the driver: every D3D8 adapter mode with w>=640 and h>=480 is kept (collection at 0x406bd7-0x406c9e in the same v1.05 build with the SafeDisc wrapper removed, read for analysis only). The retail e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll links every EnumAdapterModes result with no size or aspect filter. That dialog would therefore list 1920x1080, but the fleet launcher passes -nodialog, so players never see a resolution selector.
titles.evidence: Staged: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/MaxPayne/Play Max Payne.bat, install.reg, README-FLEET.txt; x_english.ras (DialogTexts and GCID_VIDEO strings). agent/shared/gameres.h:751-752. Disassembly: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/maxpayne_startup_dialog_modes_disasm.txt. Registry: .../registry_readback_lcd_boxes.json. The .246 frame that shows only the desktop: .../perbox-2026-08-31_246_MaxPayne_Play_Max_Payne.png.
titles.fix: There is no in-game option to fix, because the game has no in-game resolution entry. No fix is needed for 1080p: the per-box HKCU mode is already 1920x1080x32. If a visible selector is wanted, add a second launch.txt shortcut through the same mount template with GAMEARGS='-skipstartup' (without -nodialog), which exposes the startup dialog's Screen Mode list. The FLEETRES block will re-assert the panel mode on the next 'Play' launch. Do NOT stage anything from Max_Payne_Fixes.zip. Its MaxPayne.exe is a no-CD crack, and its ASI loader and WidescreenFix are PE subsystem 6.0, which XP refuses. Its e2mfc.dll and e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll byte edits, disassembled here, are code caves around plugin DllMain calls and run-once guards, not a change to the mode list.
titles.fix_source: already in tree; the optional shortcut goes through provisioning/discmount/specs/MaxPayne.json + scripts/fleet/make-mount-launcher.py + launch.txt
titles.fix_risk: Low. Single player only, so there is no multiplayer or anti-cheat impact. At 16:9 without ThirteenAG's fix the 4:3 HUD/FOV will likely be stretched (engine knowledge, unverified). The staged launcher still has VOLID=MAX_PAYNE, while README-FLEET says Windows reports the Joliet label 'Max Payne'. The 'already mounted?' probe may therefore never match and the image gets remounted on each launch (cosmetic).
titles.hw_check: On .145 (XP, DAEMON Tools): first confirm the tray menu Emulation > SafeDisc is ticked. Then EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\MaxPayne" "Play Max Payne.bat"; after about 45 s, SCREENSHOT 0 should show the main menu at 1920x1080 (XP can capture D3D8 fullscreen). Check REGREAD HKCU Software\Remedy Entertainment\Max Payne\Video Settings for 1920/1080/32. To see the selector, start MaxPayne.exe without -nodialog with the disc mounted. The startup dialog is an ordinary Win32 MFC dialog, so keyboard input (Alt+S for Screen Mode, then arrow keys) and UICLICK both work; screenshot the open combo and look for '1920 x 1080 x 32'.
titles.verifier_notes: The 1080p render on an LCD is still unproven. The compat DB rows 'MaxPayne .246 verified 1920x1080' and 'RedFaction .143 verified' come from frames showing only the desktop and are not evidence. The '.123 no mounter' row is stale: .123 now reports d347bus.

titles.title: RedFaction
titles.engine: Geo-Mod - Red Faction 1.20 (build.ver 0xB1 = 177; rf.exe md5 0ba3b15d64a702333a4d9a0815f782b7, linked 2001-09-03; Direct3D 8 loaded at run time)
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 on every box today. The mechanism exists but writes the WRONG HIVE. 'Play Red Faction.bat' lines 55-58 run FLEETRES -reg HKLM 'SOFTWARE\Volition\Red Faction' for Resolution Width, Resolution Height and Resolution Bit Depth, and gameres.h:753-755 write the same at sync. rf.exe reads these values from HKEY_CURRENT_USER. They are registered with section NULL (0x4b1480: push 0 / 'Resolution Width' / default 0x280; 'Resolution Height' default 0x1e0). The key builder 0x52b2a0 begins `mov ebp,0x80000001` and, for a NULL section, returns HKCU with 'Software\Volition\Red Faction'; RegOpenKeyExA then opens that. Read back 2026-09-29 on .123, .145, .195 and .240: HKLM holds 1920/1080/32, while HKCU holds only install.reg's UpdateRate/ForcePort/etc. and no Resolution values, so the engine falls back to its compiled 640x480. This matches the 2026-08-31 perbox frames of the Red Faction menu at 640x480 on .246 (a 1080p LCD), .133, .171 and .124. PER-TITLE-CHANGES.md had flagged 'Confirm the hive on a box that has run the game'.
titles.menu_source: rf.exe has no reachable in-game screen-resolution option. Its only resolution-list code, a set-by-index routine at 0x4b15d0 over {640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x1024} at 0x5a1298, has no call, jump or pointer reference anywhere in the image. strings.tbl #997 'Resolution:' is annotated 'As in texture resolution.' The vendor launcher RedFaction.exe (Setup > Video > Detect Available Cards) enumerates D3D8 adapter modes but records only those equal to its hardcoded table at 0x4ad5d0: 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x1024 (loops at 0x401187 and 0x40c108). 1920x1080 can never appear there. The fleet launcher bypasses RedFaction.exe and starts rf.exe directly.
titles.evidence: Disassembly: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/redfaction_rf_exe_reads_HKCU_disasm.txt. Registry: .../registry_readback_lcd_boxes.json (HKLM holds 1920/1080/32 and HKCU has no Resolution values on all four LCD boxes). Frames: .../perbox-2026-08-31_246_RedFaction_Play_Red_Faction.png and .../perbox-2026-08-31_133_RedFaction_Play_Red_Faction.png (640x480 menus). Staged: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/RedFaction/Play Red Faction.bat lines 55-58, install.reg (HKCU block), README-FLEET.txt. scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py 'RedFaction' entry; agent/shared/gameres.h:753-755.
titles.fix: (1) Change the hive. In the RedFaction entry of stage-fleetres.py, use reg_cfg('HKCU', 'SOFTWARE\Volition\Red Faction', ...), and change the root of gameres.h rules 753-755 from "HKLM" to "HKCU"; value names and DWORD types stay the same. Optionally delete the stray HKLM values. With that, rf.exe starts at FR_W x FR_H. (2) Test the HUD before pushing 1920x1080. rf.exe's HUD-coordinate selector 0x4377f0 only has blocks for widths 640, 800, 1024 and 1280 (hud.tbl #640x480..#1280x1024). At width 1920 the block at 0x637628 stays zero-filled BSS, so HUD elements are expected to be misplaced (inferred from disassembly, not observed). If the HUD is broken, the stock HUD-correct choice is 1280x1024 or 1024x768, which is not 16:9. (3) A widescreen HUD and FOV need Dash Faction (rafalh), which is not on the share. Its README says it supports Windows 7 and newer and RF 1.20 NA only, so it would help .195 alone, not the three XP LCD boxes. A 1080p entry in any menu is impossible on stock 1.20.
titles.fix_source: The hive change uses the FLEETRES.EXE already staged here (its -reg option supports HKCU) plus edits to scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py and agent/shared/gameres.h. Dash Faction would have to be downloaded from github.com/rafalh/dashfaction releases (not found on the share, case-insensitive search).
titles.fix_risk: The hive fix itself is low risk; the real risk is the 1920 HUD described above, so test on one box before pushing fleet-wide. Multiplayer: resolution is local to the client, so the stock 1.20 dedicated server is unaffected and RF has no anti-cheat. Dash Faction is client-side and joins stock servers, but it changes the launch path (DashFactionLauncher.exe) and is Win7+ only.
titles.hw_check: On .145 (XP, DAEMON Tools; RF only needs disc 2 visible, with no copy protection): after the hive fix, REGREAD HKCU SOFTWARE\Volition\Red Faction should show Resolution Width 1920 and Height 1080. Then EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\RedFaction" "Play Red Faction.bat"; SCREENSHOT 0 should be 1920x1080 (today it is 640x480). Start the first mission (NEW) and screenshot the HUD placement; the menu is mouse-driven and keyboard navigation is not established. To confirm the vendor list: LAUNCH RedFaction.exe, go to Setup > Video tab (a Win32 property sheet, so UICLICK works), press Detect Available Cards, and screenshot the resolution list; expect 1280x1024 as the maximum.
titles.verifier_notes: Registry state and disassembly agree, and agree with the 640x480 frames. The compat DB row '.143 verified 1024x768' is a desktop-only frame.

titles.title: Tribes2
titles.engine: Torque/V12 - Tribes 2 v25034.005 (2004 FilePlanet full release) + TribesNext RC2a (GameData\Tribes2.exe 4,419,584 B dated 2013-03-18); OpenGL by default, with D3D and Voodoo2 device fallbacks
titles.launch_sets: Not 1080p: the title starts at 800x600, and no resolution mechanism exists. The tree has no FLEETRES.EXE or FLEETRES.BAT, the launchers call none, gameres.h has no rule, and notes.txt says this is deliberate. No prefs\ClientPrefs.cs is staged, and none exists on .123, .145, .195 or .240 (DIRLIST 2026-09-29), so the title has never run on any LCD box. On first launch the winWindow.cc init (0x5611f9) parses $pref::Video::resolution and uses the defaults 800 (0x320) x 600 (0x258) x 16 (0x10). On first device activation the matched card profile's ProFile runs, and GeForce.cs and Radeon.cs both set $pref::Video::resolution = "800 600 32". A mode the player picks in Options persists per box in prefs\ClientPrefs.cs, which is exported on exit. notes.txt claims the engine 'picks from' the driver list; the code does not do that.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver. The Options > Video resolution popup, OP_ResMenu::init in base\scripts.vl2 scripts/OptionsDlg.cs, adds every getResolutionList(device) entry when fullscreen; only windowed mode filters to smaller than the desktop. The engine builds that list (Tribes2.exe 0x5631f5 for OpenGL, 0x567f55 for D3D) from EnumDisplaySettingsA, keeping w>=640, h>=480 and bpp 16 or 32 (and bpp equal to the desktop unless depth switching is allowed). There is no maximum and no aspect filter. $pref::Video::clipHigh removes modes above 1152x864 (0x563779), but CardProfiles.cs sets ClipHigh=true only for NVIDIA 'RIVA TNT/'. It is false for NVIDIA '*' (the GeForce 8400GS) and ATI 'Radeon' (HD 3850, HD 5450, X800).
titles.evidence: Disassembly and script excerpts: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/tribes2_resolution_list_disasm.txt. Staged: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Tribes2/GameData/base/scripts.vl2 (scripts/OptionsDlg.cs lines 746-771, scripts/clientDefaults.cs), GameData/console_start.cs (line 101 $clientprefs, lines 425-427 exec clientDefaults then prefs, line 1164 createCanvas), GameData/CardProfiles.cs, GeForce.cs and Radeon.cs ('800 600 32'), notes.txt, both Play*.bat. Box state: .../registry_readback_lcd_boxes.json (no ClientPrefs.cs anywhere).
titles.fix: No change is needed for the menu. To make the title start at 1080p without a human, stage FLEETRES.EXE and FLEETRES.BAT into Tribes2. In both launchers, before start, create GameData\base\prefs\ClientPrefs.cs if it is missing: FLEETRES -setline returns 1 and writes nothing when the file does not exist. Then run FLEETRES -setline on that file with key $pref::Video::resolution and line $pref::Video::resolution = `%FR_W% %FR_H% 32`; (console_start.cs execs prefs/clientPrefs.cs before createCanvas). On the first run the card profile, applied when defaultsVendor/defaultsRenderer are unset, may overwrite the value with 800 600 32; check whether a second launch is needed.
titles.fix_source: FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT from provisioning/fleetres (not yet in this tree) plus a new scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py entry; nothing to download
titles.fix_risk: Low: ClientPrefs.cs is per-box state that the engine rewrites, which is the same pattern already used for other titles. Two things must be checked on the box: which prefs directory the engine writes under -mod Classic (base\prefs or Classic\prefs), and whether the first-run card profile overrides the line. Multiplayer is unaffected, since resolution is local to the client and TribesNext auth is separate. The title has never been run on any fleet box, so 2001 OpenGL on current Catalyst/ForceWare drivers is itself unproven.
titles.hw_check: On .145 or .123: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Tribes2" "Play Tribes 2 Solo and LAN.bat"; on XP, SCREENSHOT should show 800x600 today. Open Options > Video > Resolution popup and screenshot the list, which should include 1920 1080. It is a Torque GUI; if absolute clicks do not land, open the console with ~ (UIKEY TILDE) and type echo(getResolutionList($pref::Video::displayDevice)); then screenshot the console. After Apply and quit, DIRLIST GameData\base\prefs and GameData\Classic\prefs, then DOWNLOAD ClientPrefs.cs and confirm $pref::Video::resolution = "1920 1080 32".
titles.verifier_notes: The menu result comes from script and engine code and holds for every fleet LCD GPU profile; it has never been observed on screen, because no box has run Tribes 2 yet.

titles.title: RainbowSix
titles.engine: Red Storm 'Sherman' engine - Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six (1998), GOG build, shell v001.04; DirectDraw + Direct3D immediate mode (software renderer selectable)
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 fullscreen on the 1080p LCDs. There is no FLEETRES in the tree and no gameres.h rule. install.reg sets FullScreen=1 and SoftwareOnly=0 but no VideoResolution, so the compiled default '640x480' (string at 0x89944c, assigned at 0x41525a) applies. Measured 2026-09-01 on .123: the main menu rendered at 640x480 (ddraw). .123's HKLM now holds VideoResolution='640x480', written by the game; .145, .195 and .240 have no value (read 2026-09-29). Every registry access in the exe uses HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (8 RegCreateKeyExA sites, all push 0x80000002).
titles.menu_source: The list is hardcoded. Options > VIDEO > RESOLUTION is a radio set taken from the pointer table at VA 0x8a53a0: '320x240 LOW', '640x480 MED', '800x600 HIGH'. Beyond that, the renderer cannot take 1080p at all. Renderer::EnumerateDisplayModes (0x46ea50) calls IDirectDraw::EnumDisplayModes with callback 0x497dd0, which drops every mode whose dwWidth > 1024 (cmp 0x400) or dwHeight > 768 (cmp 0x300) and keeps at most 50 (0x32). VideoResolution is parsed generically at 0x40e5e0 (split at 'x', atoi both halves) but must then exactly match a mode in that capped list (0x46ff7c); otherwise it fails with 'Unable to find a display mode to match request'.
titles.evidence: Disassembly: .claude/evidence-1080p/g6-farcry-bf1942-maxpayne-redfaction-tribes2-r6/rainbowsix_1024x768_cap_disasm.txt. Registry: .../registry_readback_lcd_boxes.json (VideoResolution '640x480' on .123, absent elsewhere). Frame: .../r6_123_main_menu_2026-09-01.png (640x480, v001.04). Staged: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/RainbowSix/Play Rainbow Six.bat and install.reg. Web (background only, not the binary): a GOG forum thread 'Resolution higher than 1024x768?' reports that setting VideoResolution to 1920x1080 still gives 1024x768, and PCGW says the game supports up to 1024x768 by default.
titles.fix: Stock 1.04 has no route to 1920x1080, neither through the menu nor through the registry (the 1024x768 cap at 0x497dd0). The best stock improvement is to stage FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT into RainbowSix and have 'Play Rainbow Six.bat' run `call FLEETRES.BAT -cap 1024 768` and then `FLEETRES.EXE -reg HKLM "SOFTWARE\Red Storm Entertainment\Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six" VideoResolution sz %FR_W43%x%FR_H43%`, which gives '1024x768' on the LCDs. That is 4:3, not 1080p. gameres.h has no per-title cap, so a sync-time rule would need one. True 1080p would need the unofficial PCGW 'Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six - Widescreen & FOV Fix' (AlphaYellow, community file 3438) plus ThirteenAG's Ultimate ASI Loader (as dsound.dll). Neither is on the share (case-insensitive search). The loader is PE subsystem 6.0, which XP refuses, so this would work on .195 (Win7) only. The alternative is a hand patch of the two compares at 0x497dd7/0x497ddf plus VideoResolution=1920x1080; it is untested, and other buffers and the 640x480 shell may assume a maximum of 1024x768.
titles.fix_source: 1024x768: FLEETRES from provisioning/fleetres plus a scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py entry (a GR_OP_REG rule would need a per-title cap added to agent/shared/gameres.h). 1080p: downloads from community.pcgamingwiki.com/files/file/3438 and github.com/ThirteenAG/Ultimate-ASI-Loader.
titles.fix_risk: 1024x768: low, but whether the 640x480 shell and planning screens switch cleanly to a 1024x768 mission view is unverified. The ASI route or a byte patch changes the load path or the exe, works only on Win7, and its stretch and HUD behaviour are unknown. Multiplayer (-server/-client) does not depend on resolution, and the title has no anti-cheat.
titles.hw_check: On .145 or .123: REGREAD HKLM "SOFTWARE\Red Storm Entertainment\Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six" and note VideoResolution. EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\RainbowSix" "Play Rainbow Six.bat", let intro.smk finish (ESC quits the game), then SCREENSHOT 0 the main menu (XP; 16-bit DirectDraw captures). Options > VIDEO > RESOLUTION should show only 320x240, 640x480 and 800x600. The shell draws its own cursor and keyboard navigation is not established, so it may need a human once. For the 1024x768 change: set the value, start a mission, then take a SCREENSHOT and run DISPLAYCFG get while in the mission.
titles.verifier_notes: The cap is read directly from the binary and agrees with the web report. None of the three changes (1024x768, ASI, patch) has been tried on hardware.
